qwen35.ptx

Hand-written PTX kernels for Qwen 3.5 (dense, text) inference. The whole file, as the engine loads it: each kernel and device function in a card with its parameters, resources and cross references, then its code. Every label, parameter, array and function name links to its definition; hover a register to see each of its uses in that function, click it to keep them marked.

lines 1–47
qwen35.ptx - hand-written PTX kernels for Qwen 3.5 (dense, text) inference. The model is a hybrid: of every 4 layers, 3 are Gated DeltaNet layers (linear attention with a 128 x 128 recurrent state per head) and the 4th is a gated full-attention layer. The host (qwen35.c) runs a layer as (T tokens at a time): xn = rmsnorm(x) * attn_norm rmsnorm, quant_q8 linear-attention layer: qkv | z = Wqkvz . xn (8192 | 4096) mv_* / gemm_q beta | alpha = Wba . xn (32 | 32) mv_* / gemm_q q|k|v = silu(causal conv1d over the last 4 gdn_conv (q, k heads also tokens' qkv), per channel L2-normalized), conv_save per v head h (32, 128 dims; k head h % 16): gdn_recur g = exp(softplus(alpha + dt_bias) * a), b = sigmoid(beta) S = g S + k ((v - g S^T k) b)^T, o = S^T q / sqrt(128) y = Wout . (rmsnorm(o) * ssm_norm * silu(z)) gated_norm, quant_q8, mv/gemm full-attention layer (16 q heads, 4 kv heads, 256 dims): q|gate, k, v = Wqkv . xn mv_* / gemm_q q, k = rmsnorm(head) * q|k_norm, RoPE on qk_norm_rope (k, v also to the first 64 dims the f16 KV cache) y = Wo . (softmax(q K^T / 16) V * sigmoid(gate)) attention, quant_q8, mv/gemm x += y (the matrix kernels' resid) xn = rmsnorm(x) * post_attention_norm g|u = [Wgate; Wup] . xn, h = silu(g) * u mv/gemm, swiglu x += Wdown . h mv/gemm and finally logits = Wout . rmsnorm(x) * output_norm, next = argmax. Weights are ggml's quantized blocks (see quant.h) with the fields of the 32-value types in separate arrays so every load is aligned: Q8_0: q int8 [rows][cols], d f16 [rows][cols/32] Q4_1: qs u8 [rows][cols/2] (16 bytes per block), dm f16x2 [rows][cols/32] Q5_K: the 176-byte blocks as stored, [rows][cols/256] Q6_K: ql | qh | scales (208 bytes) [rows][cols/256], d f16 [rows][cols/256] Activations entering a matrix are quantized to int8 in blocks of 32 (as llama.cpp does): xq int8 [n] and xds f32x2 [n/32] = {d, d * sum_j q_j}. A weight block with scale s and offset m (w = s q + m) then contributes s d_x dot(q_w, q_x) + m d_x sum(q_x) with exact integer dot products (dp4a in the matrix-vector kernels, int8 tensor-core mma in the GEMM).

section notelines 243–250
Matrix-vector kernels (one token): y[r] = sum_c W[r][c] * x[c] + resid[r] x as int8 blocks (xq, xds from quant_q8); resid may be 0 (null) and y may equal resid. One warp per row; lane b takes the 32-value blocks b, b+32, ..., each giving an exact integer dot product that is scaled into the lane's f32 sum; the lanes' sums are added at the end. Launch: blockDim = 256 (8 rows per block), gridDim = ceil(rows / 8).

Kernel: mv_q4_1 W in Q4_1: w = d q + m. Byte j of a block holds value j (low nibble) and value j+16 (high nibble), so word k of the 16 bytes gives values 4k..4k+3 and 16+4k..16+4k+3 - against activation words k and 4+k.

section notelines 913–935
Kernel: gemm_q Y[t][r] = sum_c W[r][c] * X[t][c] + resid[t][r] for T tokens (the prompt path). W is Q8_0 (type 0), Q4_1 (type 1) or Q5_K (type 2), in the layouts above; X is int8 blocks (Xq [T][cols], Xds [T][cols/32] from quant_q8 over the T rows). Y and resid have row stride ldy (Y can be a column slice of a wider matrix); resid may be 0 and Y may equal resid. rows % 64 == 0, cols % 64 == 0 (% 256 for Q5_K). A block computes a 64-row x 64-token tile. Per 64-wide step along the inner dimension (two 32-value blocks) it stores the weights as int8 q (Ws[row][k], rows padded to 80 bytes so the fragment loads hit 32 different banks) with each block's scale and offset (w = s q + m), and the activations' int8 (Xs[token][k]) with d and d * sum(q). Warp w takes rows 16 (w % 4) .. +15 and tokens 32 (w / 4) .. +31: per 32-value block one A fragment, four B fragments, four mma.m16n8k32 (exact int32 block dot products), each scaled into the f32 sums as acc += dot * (s_w d_x) + m_w (d_x sum q_x) in a fixed order, so a token's result doesn't depend on the others in its tile (prompt chunking doesn't change any value). Launch: blockDim = 256, gridDim = (ceil(T / 64), rows / 64) - the token tiles of one weight tile run back to back, so each weight is read from memory about once.

section notelines 1430–1435
Gated DeltaNet (linear attention) kernels. Per layer the conv state holds the last 3 tokens' qkv inputs (f32 [3][C], oldest first) and the recurrent state S the 32 heads' 128 x 128 matrices (f32 [h][i][j], i = key dim, j = value dim).
kernel

gdn_conv

lines 1445–1557
Kernel: gdn_conv out[t][c] = silu(sum_{s<4} w[c][s] x_{t-3+s}[c]) for the C channels of qkv (q 2048 | k 2048 | v 4096), where x_u is in[u] for u >= 0 and the conv state's row 3 + u before the chunk (u < 0). The first nnorm 128-channel heads (q and k) are then L2-normalized: y / sqrt(sum y^2 + eps) (llama.cpp's rms_norm(eps / 128) / sqrt(128)). Launch: gridDim = (C / 128, T), blockDim = 128.

Kernel: conv_save conv state <- the last 3 of [state (3 rows); in (T rows)] (run after gdn_conv). A thread owns a channel and writes rows 0, 1, 2 in order, so with T < 3 it reads state rows before they are overwritten. Grid-stride over the C channels.

gdn_recur

lines 1635–1834
Kernel: gdn_recur the gated delta rule over T tokens, for v head h and 32 of its 128 value columns j (k and q from head h % 16, llama.cpp's mapping), as llama.cpp's fused CUDA kernel computes it: b = sigmoid(beta_t[h]), g = exp(softplus(alpha_t[h] + dt_bias[h]) * a[h]) kv_j = sum_i S[i][j] k_i, delta_j = (v_j - g kv_j) b S[i][j] = g S[i][j] + k_i delta_j, out_j = scale * sum_i S[i][j] q_i softplus(x) = x for x > 20, else log(1 + exp(x)). The block's 128 x 32 slice of S stays in shared memory (thread j owns column j: conflict-free) for the whole chunk and is written back at the end. Launch: gridDim = (32 heads, 4), blockDim = 32.

swiglu

lines 1928–1976
Kernel: swiglu out[t][j] = silu(g[t][j]) * u[t][j] for j < n, where gu[t] = [g: n | u: n] (the gate and up halves of one matrix product). silu(x) = x / (1 + exp(-x)). Grid-stride.

Full-attention layer kernels. qkv[t] = [q|gate: nh x (256 | 256) | k: nkv x 256 | v: nkv x 256]; the KV cache is f16 [ctx][nkv][256] per layer.
kernel

qk_norm_rope

lines 1995–2215
Kernel: qk_norm_rope for token t = blockIdx.y at position pos = pos0 + t and head h = blockIdx.x (q heads, then k heads, then v heads): q and k heads: x = rmsnorm(x) * w (qw for q, kw for k), then NeoX RoPE on the first 64 dims only: pairs (i, i+32) for i < 32, x_i' = x_i cos - x_{i+32} sin, x_{i+32}' = x_i sin + x_{i+32} cos with cs[pos][i] = {cos, sin}; written back to qkv, k (as f16) also to the K cache at pos. v heads: copied to the V cache as f16. Launch: gridDim = (nh + 2*nkv, tokens), blockDim = 32. Lane l owns dims 8l..8l+7; lanes 0..3 hold the rotary dims' first halves, 4..7 the second.

kernel

attention

lines 2233–2593
Kernel: attention for query token t = blockIdx.y at position p = pos0 + t and q head h = blockIdx.x, over the cached keys j in [lo, p]: out_h = sum_j softmax_j(scale * q_h . k_j) v_j lo = p - window + 1 for sliding-window layers (window != 0), else 0. Key j lives in cache slot j % slots (a ring when slots < positions); grouped-query: q head h reads kv head h / (nh / nkv). Heads have 256 dims, q head h at h * qhs in its token's row. With gate != 0 the output is multiplied by sigmoid(gate_h), the 256 values after q head h. Launch: gridDim = (nh, tokens), blockDim = 256 (8 warps). Warp w takes keys lo+w, lo+w+8, ..., two per step (keys i and i+8), keeping an online softmax: running max m and sum l of exp(s - m), accumulator of exp(s - m) v (scores in log2 units, so exp is ex2). Lane l owns dims 8l..8l+7. At the end the 8 warps' (m, l, acc) are merged through shared memory and thread d writes out dim d.

compact_logits

lines 2703–2760
Kernel: compact_logits gathers the sampling candidates: every i with x[i] >= x[best] - margin, where best is argmax's result. out[0] = count (may exceed cap: then only cap entries are stored and the host falls back to the full logits), out[2 + 2j] = index, out[3 + 2j] = logit (f32 bits). The host zeroes out[0] first. Grid-stride.

sample_logits

lines 2772–2912
Kernel: sample_logits draws a token from softmax(x / T) over the whole vocabulary, optionally without tokens whose weight relative to the best is below min_w (min-p), by inverse CDF in index order: w_i = exp((x_i - x_best) / T) (0 if w_i < min_w), Z = sum_i w_i, pick the i where the running sum of w first exceeds u * Z. out[0] = the token, out[1] = Z (f32 bits; also used by the host for top-p). u in [0, 1) comes from the host's seeded RNG. Launch: one block of 1024 threads; thread t owns a contiguous chunk.
